subject: EduScan drift analysis silently lies: two snapshot formats share one history directory
description: Found 2026-09-27 running a full scan with --diff. It reported 'Trend: REGRESSING, Issues 0 -> 14594 (+14594)', which is an ARTIFACT, not a regression. _tools/reports/history/ contains snapshots from two different writers with incompatible schemas: EduScan's own (named scan-<ISO>T<time>.json, keys issues/meta/summary/syncStatus, carrying the full issues array) and another producer's (named scan-<date>_<time>.json with UNDERSCORE, keys catalog/content/filesScanned/highByHouse/rules/scanDuration/sync, carrying NO issues array). The diff picks the most recent file by timestamp; when that happens to be an underscore-format snapshot it reads issues as absent, treats it as 0, and reports every current finding as NEW. Verified by reading the three newest files: 14594 issues, then 0 issues with the foreign schema, then 14595. WHY IT MATTERS: drift is the mechanism that distinguishes 'a rule newly fired' from 'legacy inventory', which is exactly the judgement post-verify and the deploy gates depend on, and the failure is SILENT - it prints a confident trend either way. It also means a REAL regression would be indistinguishable from this noise. FIX OPTIONS: have the diff skip snapshots whose schema lacks an issues array rather than scoring them as zero; or give the two producers separate directories; or make the foreign writer stop landing in EduScan's history dir. The first is the smallest and fails safe. NOT urgent for students, but it quietly degrades every gate that reasons about drift.
activeForm: Working on: EduScan drift analysis silently lies: two snapshot formats share one history directory
